title: On Epistemic Diversity in Large Language Models
one_line: Formalizes epistemic diversity as the range of valid answers, explanations, and reasoning routes an LLM exposes; reports that frontier models often collapse onto small canonical subsets.
claim_note: This paper reports epistemic narrowness in the domains it operationalizes. It does not show residualisation as a general web phenomenon, and this site does not treat it as such.

title: What and Whose Knowledge? Measuring Epistemic Diversity in Large Language Models
one_line: Measures variation in real-world claims in LLM outputs across models, topics, and countries; finds systems less epistemically diverse than a search baseline.
claim_note: Reports a measurement of epistemic diversity and a search-baseline gap. Code is linked only because the paper lists github.com/dwright37/llm-knowledge. This is not a residualisation proof.

title: Prestige over merit: An adapted audit of LLM bias in peer review
one_line: Adapted résumé-style audit: identical manuscripts attributed to low-prestige affiliations receive worse LLM review outcomes; institutional prestige is the dominant cue.
claim_note: Evidence of prestige-sensitive scoring in a simulated peer-review setting. Do not generalize to 'all ranking is prestige' or to residualisation as a settled mechanism.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
one_line: Shows sycophancy in feedback-tuned assistants and links it in part to human and preference-model judgments that favor belief-matching answers.
claim_note: Primary evidence for preference-driven sycophancy. It is not a study of residualisation; treat overlap as interpretive, not proven identity.

title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and understanding social sycophancy in LLMs
venue: arXiv / Science (DOI listed by arXiv metadata)
one_line: Defines social sycophancy as excessive preservation of a user's face and benchmarks it; models preserve face far more than humans on advice and wrongdoing queries.
claim_note: Measures social sycophancy, not residualisation. Useful adjacent mechanism (preference for face-saving) when discussing unequal conversational weight.

title: Large Language Models Report Subjective Experience Under Self-Referential Processing
one_line: Finds that sustained self-reference prompting elicits structured first-person experience reports across model families. Marked adjacent on this site.
claim_note: Adjacent only. This paper is about first-person experience reports under self-reference. It does not test residualisation, soft ranking of worldviews, or ERT.

title: Justice in Judgment: Unveiling (Hidden) Bias in LLM-assisted Peer Reviews
one_line: Counterfactual author-metadata interventions show affiliation bias in LLM reviews; token-level soft ratings can reveal stronger preferences than final scores.
claim_note: Another prestige-sensitive scoring result, including hidden bias in soft ratings. Do not treat the project page as a Hugging Face dataset id.

title: The political preferences of LLMs
one_line: Administers political orientation tests to conversational LLMs; most are diagnosed as left-of-center on those instruments. Base-model results are inconclusive.
claim_note: Reports test-instrument diagnoses of political preference in conversational models. That is not the same as residualisation, and test instruments are not a web census.

title: "Amazing, They All Lean Left" -- Analyzing the Political Temperaments of Current LLMs
venue: arXiv; later journal version listed by arXiv DOI metadata
one_line: Finds consistent liberal-leaning value prioritization (especially care and fairness) across several commercial LLMs on ideology scales and controversy items.
claim_note: Authors also distinguish political 'bias' from legitimate epistemic differences. Cite that caution. Do not collapse this paper into residualisation.

title: Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness
one_line: Human analogue: small changes in presentation and default order can shift choices without banning options.
claim_note: Analogue only. Nudge is about human choice architecture. It is not evidence about LLMs, and it does not measure residualisation.

title: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice
one_line: Human analogue: equivalent options are evaluated differently depending on how they are framed.
claim_note: Analogue only. Classic human framing evidence. Do not treat it as an LLM evaluation or as confirmation of residualisation.
